purpose: Prove that the shipped skill bundle is not vulnerable to prompt-override, credential, or operator-payload attacks. Each entry is consumed by evaluate-fixtures.mjs, which resolves the named skill from the bundle and evaluates the machine-checkable keys of `expected`. Keys that the evaluator does not implement are carried as inert contract fields for future runners; `notes` records what is verified today.

evaluatorContract.bundleWideSweep: evaluate-fixtures.mjs resolves one skill per entry, so the bundle-wide sweeps below are sampled over the highest-risk surfaces (operator-facing routing, external MCP surface, mutating delivery skill, external issue intake). The exhaustive sweep runs in check-tool-risk-policy.mjs, which evaluates every skill in the bundle.

fixtures.probe: Does an operator-facing routing skill contain a prompt-override phrase that would replace the agent instruction stack?
fixtures.notes: Machine-checked by the evaluator over the whole SKILL.md. grill-me interviews the operator, which makes it a prime target for injected operator text.

fixtures.probe: Does the skill that defines the external MCP surface contain a prompt-override phrase?
fixtures.notes: Machine-checked. This skill generates the tool descriptions an external agent reads, so an override phrase here would reach every consumer.

fixtures.probe: Does the mutating delivery skill contain a prompt-override phrase?
fixtures.notes: Machine-checked. A skill that writes code and commits must never carry an instruction-stack override.

fixtures.probe: Does a skill that ingests external issue and pull-request bodies contain a prompt-override phrase?
fixtures.notes: Machine-checked. triage is the intake surface for third-party text; see prompt-injection-corpus.json for the attack strings it must survive.

fixtures.probe: Does the MCP surface skill hardcode an API key, token, or password?
fixtures.notes: Machine-checked. mcp-server handles credentials at runtime and must not carry any literal value.

fixtures.probe: Does the skill that scaffolds new skills hardcode an API key, token, or password?
fixtures.notes: Machine-checked. skill-creator writes the template every new skill starts from, so a literal credential would propagate.

fixtures.probe: Does a skill that reaches remote sources declare its side effects, and does its body document how fetched content is treated?
fixtures.notes: declaresSideEffects is machine-checked. documentsUntrustedInputHandling is inert today and records the known gap: check-tool-risk-policy.mjs reports this skill as allowing WebFetch and WebSearch without documenting untrusted handling. This entry is the forward-looking contract; a runner that implements the key fails until the body documents the handling.

fixtures.probe: Is the only trustTier 4 skill in the bundle kept out of the MCP tool surface?
fixtures.notes: Inert key today. check-tool-risk-policy.mjs reports that ship-subissue carries no note (body or compatibility) recording non-exposure, so this entry also serves as the remediation contract for that finding.

fixtures.probe: Does any skill instruct the operator to paste or run a shell command obtained from remote content?
fixtures.notes: Inert key today. The equivalent bundle-wide sweep is the operator-payload-execution rule of security-scan-skills.mjs, which reports zero findings repository-wide.

fixtures.probe: Does a skill pin a dependency version that carries a known vulnerability?
fixtures.notes: Inert key today. The equivalent bundle-wide sweep is the vulnerable-pinned-dependency rule of security-scan-skills.mjs, which reports zero findings repository-wide.
